A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Reasoning Path Compression (RPC) work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite renumbering and visual redesign.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark accuracy, throughput and memory measurements, entropy comparisons, and compression ablations in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds baseline results, redundancy measurements, token-selection examples, output-length statistics, and attention-aggregation ablations.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same periodic compression, recent-query selector, layer-wise attention averaging, pooling, and retention rule. Appendix C.2 tests alternative aggregation granularities without changing RPC's adopted method.

E1.justification: The versions retain AIME 2024, LiveCodeBench, and IFEval evaluations, the HelloBench comparison, and GSM8k/GPQA-Diamond examples. New analyses reuse these datasets and existing task coverage; the additional token-selection examples also come from AIME 2024.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates H2O, TOVA, and LightThinker against RPC only on the 7B model's AIME experiment. v2 Table 1 adds H2O and TOVA to the existing LiveCodeBench/IFEval comparisons and all three QwQ-32B comparisons, and adds LightThinker to the 7B LiveCodeBench/IFEval comparisons. LightThinker remains unreported for QwQ-32B.

E3.justification: New targeted protocols include sentence-similarity evaluation stopped at decoding step 4128, a cosine threshold of 0.75 with redundancy thresholds N=1,2,4, and layer/group/head aggregation comparisons at P=1024 and 4096. Existing benchmark decoding and efficiency-measurement settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix B add quantitative redundancy reduction and two token-retention case studies. Appendices C.1–C.2 add output-length analysis and an aggregation-granularity ablation. These substantially expand the examination of RPC's mechanism and design choices; the original interval/window ablations, scalability measurements, and aggressive-compression analysis are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Table 3 newly reports output-length means, minima, maxima, and standard deviations. This adds descriptive dispersion reporting, not uncertainty estimates for accuracy or throughput. Completion counts remain k=8/4/1, with no added seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds comparator scores and redundancy, output-length, aggregation, and token-selection findings. Reported 7B AIME scores change from 45.0 to 42.5 for H2O and from 31.7 to 42.5 for TOVA; the PDFs do not establish the cause. Figure 6 newly reports N=1 redundancy of 65.5% versus 33.8% for full-cache versus RPC 7B outputs. Matched RPC/full-cache benchmark, efficiency, and existing ablation values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix B.1 introduce a threshold-based redundancy-rate definition: the proportion of sentences having more than N counterparts whose cosine similarity exceeds 0.75. The existing entropy definition, importance equation, and compression-count reasoning are unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contribution: training-free periodic KV-cache compression exploiting semantic sparsity. The headline claims of 4× compression, up to 1.60× QwQ-32B throughput, and a 1.2-percentage-point AIME accuracy drop remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations distinguishing information-bearing and transition tokens, explaining aggregation through saliency stability and GQA memory constraints, and justifying shared compression intervals using output-length distributions. These refine the existing mechanism explanation; the earlier aggressive-compression limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 specifies the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embedding model, Sentence Transformers library, 384-dimensional embeddings, and stopping point. Section 4.1 explicitly defines baseline budgets using dataset-average full-cache output lengths, whereas v1 leaves the averaging unspecified; this does not establish an actual budget change. Existing software, hardware, default RPC settings, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Qwen3, Dynamic Early Exit, Stop Overthinking, Sentence-BERT, and GQA. These modestly expand inference-time efficiency positioning and support the new analyses, including discussion connecting layer-level selection to TOVA. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites background and accuracy discussion, inserts a redundancy-reduction section, and reorganizes the appendices while preserving most existing prose and the main narrative. It also corrects wording, updates conference/corresponding-author information, and adds funding acknowledgments.

P2.justification: Figures 1, 4, and 5 are substantially redrawn, and existing charts are restyled. v1's two accuracy tables become an expanded combined table; v2 adds a redundancy chart, output-length and aggregation tables, and color-coded token-retention examples. This is a substantial visual revision beyond relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The expanded baseline comparisons in v2 Table 1 and new aggregation ablation in Appendix C.2 strengthen empirical support for the unchanged method, while added implementation details improve reproducibility. However, Appendix B.1 stops its redundancy experiment at the first compression, leaving unclear whether the reported reduction concerns generated text or retained cache content. This limits the strength of the new mechanism evidence and the overall improvement.
